text:
ana: quick follow-up from the sharded-residency ledger prototype i ran this morning — short thread w/ results, oddities, and next steps :mag:

vikram: nice name. what's a "ledger" in this context?

ana: (i'm ana :) the idea: instead of per-page tags or coarse granule tags, we shard residency metadata into a compact, append-only ledger partitioned by slot-range. each partition stores short entries (owner_id, residency_state, seq) and we periodically compact into a dense bitmap for fast reads. goal was to reduce metadata overhead while keeping accurate ownership for mixed tenancy and to enable cheap provenance queries.

lia: concrete numbers?

ana: ran 48h mixed-tenants canary on 6 hosts, workload = sparse embeddings + interleaved small-batch chat. baseline=per-page tags; proto=sharded-ledger w/ 64KB slot buckets and ledger compaction every 2s. observations: p50 unchanged, p95 improved slightly (~4ms) for embedding-heavy tenants, host memory overhead dropped ~3.8% vs per-page, and NVMe small-write rate dropped ~33%. odd case: very small single-tenant models (<6MB) saw slight p95 regressions (~+10ms) in the worst windows.

vikram: how big is the ledger write rate? does it add IO pressure?

ana: metadata writes are mostly in-memory appends — we only persist compacted checkpoints to local metadata store every 2s. the append rate peaked at ~1200 entries/s/node during synthetic bursts but compaction kept the stable footprint small.

lia: how do you handle concurrent updates when many lanes touch the same slot-range?

ana: ledger is append-only and entries are cheap. readers compute residency by scanning the tail of the local partition (bounded by seq window). writers append with CAS to the tail pointer; we avoid fine-grained CAS per-slot. compaction is done by a background thread that collapses recent entries into a dense per-slot summary under an epoch fence. if readers detect epoch mismatch they consult the tail before deciding eviction.

ops-bot: note: add SLI for "ledger-append-latency" and an alert for sustained >50ms.

vikram: race/failure modes? what if compaction crashes mid-way and we have mixed old/new formats?

ana: compaction uses a two-phase checkpoint: write compacted blob -> publish new epoch -> retire old tail. on crash, restart path can reconstruct compacted state by replaying tail entries up to published epoch. we keep a tiny op-log (~4KB/min typical) to bound replay time. still want a formal recovery proof.

lia: interesting. what encoding did you use for entries? worried about per-entry blowup.

ana: entry = 12 bytes: 4B slot_base_idx, 1B owner_id, 1B state, 4B seq_ts, 2B flags. we delta-encode slot_base_idx in the on-disk checkpoint to compress long runs. measured compressed checkpoint ~120KB/node for typical canary.

vikram: the small-model regressions — hypothesize?

ana: root cause looks like the tail-scan window. small models touch few slots so the cost of consulting tail entries (scan) dominates vs direct per-page reads. mitigation: short-circuit for tiny footprints: if estimated footprint < 8MB, consult dense checkpoint directly and skip tail scan. added detector in runtime.

lia: how do hints integrate? can other layers emit residency hints into the ledger?

ana: yes — API: a tiny hint envelope that appends a provenance entry to the partition with a TTL and source tag. rough sketch:

```
Hint { slot_base, owner_id, state_enum, ttl_ms, source_enum }
```

Emitters: model compiler, request router, cache layer. ledger merges hints naturally by append order.

vikram: TTL semantics? we don't want stale provenance lingering and blocking demote.

ana: TTL is advisory for background compactor: entry older than ttl is ignored during compact-snapshot unless renewed. eviction still consults per-slot state from the latest visible checkpoint + tail. TTLs help ephemeral request-level hints not pollute long-term ownership.

lia: instrumentation? ops needs ways to debug when ledger disagrees with physical page mappings.

ana: added telemetry: ledger_checkpoint_age, tail_scan_ops_per_sec, hint_reenforce_rate, mismatched_owner_samples (periodic sampling comparing ledger owner -> kernel page owner). playbook item: when mismatched_owner_samples > 0.5% over 2m, run immediate sample and optionally force recompact.

ops-bot: recorded: add CLI to force-compact a partition and to snapshot tail for postmortem.

vikram: what's the rollback plan if we see unexpected regressions at scale?

ana: plan A: tenant-scoped fallback — flip tenant to "dense-only" mode via config service which makes runtime consult latest checkpoint only (no tail scan). Plan B: global kill switch to disable ledger and re-enable per-page metadata. Both config flips are immediate and use leadership lease semantics to avoid oscillation. cooldown=10m to re-enable.

lia: cost model? any unit-econ on metadata overhead vs eviction savings?

ana: quick calc: metadata delta saves ~0.033 evicts/sec/node on average -> translates to ~0.9 GPU-hours/month saved per heavy tenant on our measured workloads. at current committed GPU rate that is approx $X/tenant-month (i'll post precise numbers in the RFC append).

vikram: one more big picture: we must standardize the residency-hint envelope so compilers, routers, and batching layers use same fields. also explicit allowed transitions (e.g., ADVISORY->RESIDENT only, never RESIDENT->ADVISORY). can you draft proto and transition table?

ana: yes — proto sketch posted above, will add transition matrix and GC semantics in RFC follow-up. next actions: 1) add tiny short-circuit for small footprints, 2) formal recovery proof for compaction, 3) unit-econ numbers, 4) proto + transition table + ops playbook. ping @vikram @lia for review. :thumbsup:
